ble.notes: mask-go discovers masks by local-name prefix "MASK" (names look like "MASK-XXXXXX", last 6 MAC-derived) — a second discovery signal besides the fff0 service UUID.

device.name: Shining Mask
device.notes:
LED face mask with 2074 RGB LEDs, 16-pixel-tall display. All commands to the Command characteristic are AES-128 ECB encrypted with the fixed key 32672f7974ad43451d9c6c894a0e8764 (published verbatim in four independent sources: GoneUp/mask-go, BishopFox/shining-mask, BrickCraftDream/Shining-Mask-stuff, Staars' gist). No pairing/authentication. Image data to the upload characteristic is sent unencrypted. FCC ID: 2AOLN-16. Color order for the FC (foreground color) command is R,G,B per every public implementation (mask-go, tayred06, BrickCraftDream) — an earlier R,B,G reading rested on private APK analysis only and still needs on-hardware A/B verification (existing clients only set white, so a G/B swap would be invisible to them). CONFIDENCE: command structure and AES key HIGH (well-documented in open-source shining-mask implementations, package cn.com.heaton.shiningmask); FC color order MEDIUM pending the hardware A/B test. Security: Bishop Fox ("Invasion of the Face Changers", 2025-10-30) showed anyone within ~10 m can take over a mask; no fix is expected (no firmware-update channel). Hardware RE (adrihd/ShiningAppMask-ReverseEngineering, 2026-01): Artery AT32F415 MCU, Jieli BP27387 BLE SoC, 16 MB PY25Q128HA SPI flash. Decrypted OTA firmware images (TR1906R04-*) and a full flash dump are archived in the research repo (/home/claude/research/shining-mask/firmware/).
Enrich-branch evidence: the official Shining Mask Android package cn.com.heaton.shiningmask was inspected from APKPure XAPK v1.2.6/versionCode 126, SHA256 29cc2c088634b28b06b67cab7b17f15bb6551bdb3d422b4e188274c825fbcb94. Static analysis and public RE agree on service 0000fff0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb holding the d44bc439 characteristics: command d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129600, notification characteristic d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129601, image/text upload characteristic d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-92541612960a, audio visualizer characteristic d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-92541612960b, and CCCD 00002902-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb. Public sources include GoneUp/mask-go, BrickCraftDream/Shining-Mask-stuff, BishopFox/shining-mask, the Bishop Fox Bluetooth LED mask write-up, and Staars' Shining Mask gist. Text/bitmap upload uses DATS, REOK acknowledgements, 98-byte chunks when MTU is set (an 18-byte fallback when MTU is not negotiated is unverified — no public source documents it), and DATCP/DATCPOK completion.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control — Bishop Fox (2025-10-30) demonstrated unauthenticated takeover within ~10 m, and no fix is expected (the device has no firmware-update channel).

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No provisioning. Commands are AES-encrypted with a fixed key, so any client that implements the framing can connect straight away.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

set_foreground_color.description: Set text foreground color. Channels are emitted in R,G,B order — as the template below states — per every public implementation (mask-go SetTextFrontColor, tayred06 mask_controller.py, BrickCraftDream ble-protocol.md). NOTE: needs on-hardware A/B verification — existing clients only set white, so a G/B swap would be invisible to them; the earlier R,B,G reading rested on private APK analysis only.

set_mode.description: Set display mode. 0=off, 1=steady, 2=blink, 3=scroll R-to-L, 4=scroll L-to-R, 5=steady custom

characteristics.name: Command
characteristics.notes: onEncrypt() AES-128-ECB with a fixed key is applied before every write to this characteristic. The key is published verbatim in four independent sources (GoneUp/mask-go aes.go, BishopFox code.py, BrickCraftDream ble-protocol.md, Staars gist). Confidence: HIGH.

services.name: Shining Mask Service
services.notes: Advertised primary service holding the d44bc439 command/transfer characteristics — both GATT-modeling implementations (GoneUp/mask-go, BishopFox/shining-mask) place them inside 0000fff0, so the earlier QPP-style standalone d44bc439-...-9600 service block was dropped.
